summary: Tested Reports/Exports/Morning-summary feature. New suite tests/test_iteration10_reports.py (36 tests): 35 pass, 1 fails (cron endpoint returns 500 for a non-object JSON body). Admin endpoints were tested in-process with httpx ASGITransport and an admin_user dependency override, plus public-URL 401 checks. Results: export zip has the 5 expected files and no _id; the spreadsheet endpoint and the orders_xlsx builder work (header, one row per order, blank row, totals row counting only paid orders, IST dates such as 20:00 UTC -> 01:30 AM next day, Status labels); PUT settings accepts 0/7/8/9 and returns 422 for 6/10/12/-1/'8'/null; GET settings saves site_url from an https Origin; send-summary was mocked; run_scheduled_summary gating works (sends only at the chosen hour, never twice in one day, off when 0, sends again if last sent yesterday); summary_email passes _assert_safe_email for quiet and busy days, with and without a dashboard URL, and escapes HTML; daily_stats counts are correct; cron returns 401 for no or wrong bearer, 400 for invalid JSON or a missing run id, accepted then duplicate for a repeated id, and accepts run_id in the body; crons.yml meets the contract. Full regression: 213/215 in parallel. One failure is the new bug; the other is a flaky test_discounts order-count check caused by xdist parallelism (16/16 pass serially). Frontend: compiles, storefront shows 30 product cards, /admin shows the signed-out Sign in wall, Reports section is not shown, no page errors. The signed-in Reports UI was code-reviewed only, because Clerk owner login is not available.

minor.issue: Valid bearer with a JSON body that is not an object (e.g. [1,2] or "str") gives 500 AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get' at server.py:543 `(body or {}).get(...)`. Fix: `if not isinstance(body, dict): body = {}`, or return 400.

summary_sent_on is only set after send_email succeeds, and the check and the set are not atomic. Low risk with one cron per hour, but an atomic find_one_and_update claim on summary_sent_on would make it airtight. A failed send is not retried that hour (logged only).

issues: saveBlob calls URL.revokeObjectURL right after a.click(). This can cancel the download in Safari/Firefox; defer it with setTimeout.
Time-option buttons are not disabled while a PUT is in flight (minor).
